identity.title: Artificial Hivemind: The Open-Ended Homogeneity of Language Models (and Beyond)

problem.claim: Language models often generate insufficiently diverse, human-like creative content, creating concern about homogenization of human thought.

gap.claim: Scalable evaluation of language-model output diversity remains limited, particularly for broad open-ended tasks and comparisons beyond repeated sampling from one model.

contributions.claim: Introduces Infinity-Chat, a dataset of 26K diverse real-world open-ended queries without a single ground-truth answer.
Introduces a taxonomy spanning 6 top-level categories and 17 subcategories of open-ended prompts.
Uses Infinity-Chat to study mode collapse and characterize intra-model repetition and stronger inter-model homogeneity in open-ended generation.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors describe Infinity-Chat as the first large-scale resource for systematically studying real-world open-ended queries, and their taxonomy as the first comprehensive taxonomy of the full prompt spectrum.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report pronounced Artificial Hivemind effects: one model repeatedly produces similar responses, while different models produce strikingly similar outputs.
The authors report that Infinity-Chat contains 31,250 human annotations, including absolute ratings and pairwise preferences, with 25 independent annotations per example.

The authors report poorer calibration of state-of-the-art language models, reward models, and language-model judges to human ratings when annotator preferences are idiosyncratic, despite comparable overall quality.

narrative_sequence.summary: The abstract identifies limited creative diversity and possible thought homogenization as the motivating concern.
It notes that scalable diversity evaluation is especially limited for open-ended prompts and cross-model comparisons.
The authors introduce Infinity-Chat and a 6-category, 17-subcategory taxonomy, with extensive human annotations.
The resource supports reported analyses of Artificial Hivemind effects and calibration gaps around idiosyncratic human preferences.

source_observation.claim: The abstract pairs a broad open-ended query resource with a structured taxonomy and both absolute and pairwise human judgments.

lessons.interpretation: This combination makes diversity, preference variation, and evaluation alignment distinct but jointly analyzable.
lessons.application: For a broad-generation study, define a prompt taxonomy and collect multiple judgment formats per example so diversity and evaluator alignment can be reported separately.
lessons.exception: This may be unsuitable when prompts have objective ground truth or when annotation budgets cannot support repeated judgments.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the evaluated models, diversity metrics, statistical analyses, or calibration procedure.
It does not quantify the reported homogeneity, calibration differences, or the evidence connecting these findings to long-term AI safety risks.
